features.name: AI agents for integration design
features.description: Using AI agents trained with BC quality knowledge base to understand good and bad practices in Business Central integrations, automating the design and implementation of integration extensions.
caveats: Requires custom knowledge base setup
Agent outputs need validation

features.name: BC quality knowledge base
features.description: A community and Microsoft-built repository containing skills and knowledge about good and bad practices in Business Central integrations, used to train AI agents.
caveats: Custom integration knowledge needs to be added separately
Planned for pull request to Microsoft repo

features.name: Spec-driven development for integrations
features.description: Using a brief document containing requirements, localization context, goals, constraints, and external API documentation to drive agent-based generation of technical design and roadmap.
caveats: Requires manual brief creation initially
Agent creates design based on provided specs

features.name: Information flow visualization
features.description: A diagram-based approach to visualize which systems own which data sets, where data originates, and how it flows through the integration landscape to serve as a center point for integration discussions and change management.
caveats: Needs ongoing updates as new systems are added

features.name: Integration message layer
features.description: A single table-based layer for all inbound and outbound data flows in integrations, enabling testing, debugging, logging, and error handling without depending on external systems.
caveats: Only for pushing data into BC, not reading
Requires interface pattern implementation

features.name: Integration message table with interface pattern
features.description: A table design using AL interfaces to handle different message types, with primary key not dependent on sequencing, human-readable document number, type field, and status tracking for extensible message handling.
caveats: Requires AL interface implementation
Response field for instantaneous external service response

features.name: Duplicate detection and handling
features.description: A mechanism to handle duplicate messages that occur commonly in integrations due to acknowledgement requirements and job queue crashes, preventing duplicate posting of documents.
caveats: Duplicate handling is fundamental and must be on the platform from the first day

features.name: Idempotency key pattern
features.description: Using a key-based approach to ensure that when a message with the same key arrives, the system returns the same response instead of posting a duplicate, preventing double-posting of sales orders or other documents.
caveats: Currently no platform mechanism to avoid double posting in Business Central

features.name: Error classification system
features.description: A system that classifies errors at runtime instead of just logging them, routing errors to appropriate owners (integration partner, finance, logistics) based on error type, and growing a database of error patterns.
caveats: Error classification is typically handled by integration partners on their side

features.name: Notification dispatcher service
features.description: A background service that analyzes failed messages, extracts error content, compares against an integration error table, and classifies errors with error codes or creates new patterns, enabling automated error response.

features.name: Delayed reply pattern
features.description: A pattern allowing responses to requests to be delayed when processing takes time or requires human approval, maintaining integration without breaking it and preserving visibility and traceability.

features.name: Correlation ID mechanism
features.description: Using correlation IDs to contextually join multiple messages into one conversation, allowing external services to match responses to original requests and enabling asynchronous acknowledgement through message table queries.

features.name: Durable workflows in Business Central
features.description: A pattern inspired by Azure durable functions that breaks large integration processes into small atomic operations committed in sequence, allowing the system to resume from the same state if something fails rather than restarting everything.
caveats: Applied through job queues and integration messages
Inspired by but not yet a native Business Central feature

features.name: Integration message workflow pattern
features.description: Using integration messages with job queues to handle sequences of operations like pulling orders, validating, and creating, where each type of operation is processed separately allowing individual fixes without re-running the whole process.
caveats: Requires manual setup of job queues and integration message types

features.name: Inbound webhooks via integration service
features.description: Using a middleware integration service to handle external webhooks and convert them to integration messages, since Business Central cannot directly listen to external endpoints or accept unauthenticated API calls.
caveats: Requires separate integration service infrastructure
Business Central cannot be an inbound webhook listener

features.name: Polling with incremental reads
features.description: A polling pattern that uses a setup table to track the last pull timestamp, allowing the system to request only new data from the source since the last run rather than re-fetching everything.
caveats: Requires discipline in design to avoid common polling mistakes

features.name: Stage and exit pattern for polling
features.description: A polling pattern that separates concerns by having the job queue only fetch data and insert it into a staging table, without doing any processing, validation, or workflow triggering in the same job.
caveats: Requires separate job queues for processing stages

features.name: Idempotency key for polling
features.description: Using an idempotency key mechanism to ensure that even if a polling job queue crashes mid-operation, duplicate records are not created in the system.
caveats: Requires external system or BC to support idempotency keys

features.name: Business events for outbound integration
features.description: Using Business Events as a platform-recommended way to send data out of Business Central, with lightweight notifications and the ability to add multiple subscriptions without code changes.
features.status_evidence_quote: Unfortunately, still in preview after a couple of years as well.
caveats: Still in preview despite years of availability
Requires replica instance for data payload requests

features.name: Business events with read replica
features.description: Business events send lightweight notifications; when external systems need the full payload, they request it from a Business Central read replica rather than the production tenant, preventing user experience disruption.
caveats: Requires setting up a read replica for integration workloads

features.name: Business events multi-system subscription
features.description: Once a Business Event is published, additional system subscriptions can be created using PowerShell scripts without requiring any code changes to Business Central.

features.name: Business events for integrations
features.description: Business events enable decoupled integrations by allowing external systems to subscribe to events without tight coupling to Business Central, supporting multi-system scenarios like managing multiple Shopify stores.
features.status_evidence_quote: I think we know the reason why it's still in preview. It's not instantaneously.
caveats: Delivery delays can exceed 5 minutes in some cases, making it unsuitable for real-time inventory synchronization scenarios

features.name: Outbound business events limitations
features.description: External systems consuming business events face limitations: most lack handshake capability, payloads are notification-only requiring callback to BC, and data is BC-shaped requiring transformation for other systems.
caveats: External systems require integration partners to handle webhook conversion and payload transformation

features.name: Integration message tables pattern
features.description: Store integration requests in a message table instead of making direct HTTP calls during posting, allowing posting to complete quickly while background jobs handle delivery to external systems.
caveats: Requires additional messaging infrastructure and AL code for background job orchestration

features.name: Idempotency keys for integration messages
features.description: Add message IDs to integration requests as headers so external systems can detect and reject duplicate messages, preventing duplicate processing if retries occur.
caveats: Not all external services support idempotency key concepts

features.name: Retry configuration for integration messages
features.description: Integration message types can be configured with automatic retry logic at the platform layer, such as retrying every 5 minutes up to 99 times without per-message AL code.

features.name: External integration services instead of job queues
features.description: Discussion of using external platforms like Azure integration services or re-state for orchestrating integrations, as Business Central is not an integration service and using patterns in BC is considered a workaround.
caveats: Business Central proper error handling is difficult
BC is not designed as an integration service

features.name: BC quality knowledge base repo
features.description: A Microsoft-initiated benchmark repository that stores data and knowledge for AI agents, with Microsoft, community, and custom folders for shared and organization-specific integration knowledge.

features.name: Community integration public GitHub repo
features.description: A public repository on GitHub that brings BC quality as a submodule with custom knowledge and skills organized for integration patterns, available as a template for organizations.

features.name: Good and bad knowledge patterns for agents
features.description: Documentation in the community integration repo that provides patterns for agents, including bad practices to avoid and good practices to follow, with context on why patterns are recommended.
caveats: Agents may overuse patterns without understanding when not to apply them

features.name: Agent skills documentation with architectural decisions
features.description: Skills documentation that contains architectural level decisions, version information, and direct call approaches to other systems that agents can use as templates for integration work.

features.name: Spec-driven development with agents
features.description: Development approach where an agent reads business requirements, skills, and knowledge to generate a complete technical specification and implementation plan for integrations.
caveats: Requires comprehensive knowledge base before agents can be effective

features.name: Agent-generated technical documentation
features.description: AI agents can generate comprehensive technical documentation including architectural reviews, data models, integration patterns, and identified concerns based on the brief and knowledge base.

features.name: Integration message layer pattern
features.description: Architectural pattern using an external integration layer that works with BC API pages to write integration messages, rather than writing messages directly into BC.

features.name: Agent-generated feature breakdown and plans
features.description: AI agents generate structured feature plans with sections for approach, specs, and tasks, breaking down integration projects into manageable features with architectural decisions documented.

features.name: Message handler interface pattern
features.description: Architecture pattern where a message handler interface is implemented for each new message processing requirement, avoiding the need for separate case statements in BC.

features.name: AI-generated extension code
features.description: AI agents can automatically generate complete extension projects with multiple AL objects including interfaces, enums, and data models based on specifications and knowledge base patterns.
caveats: Generated code requires review before deployment
Cannot confirm correctness without running it

features.name: Living knowledge base refinement
features.description: Knowledge base documents should be continuously updated after each integration or process to capture learnings and improvements, enabling better agent-generated output in future runs.

features.name: Agent error correction and knowledge update
features.description: When agents generate incorrect code patterns, developers can ask agents to fix both the generated code and the underlying knowledge base, preventing similar mistakes in future agent-driven work.

features.name: BC quality repository for integrations
features.description: A community-driven repository for sharing integration knowledge and best practices that developers can contribute to and use for building integrations more efficiently.
caveats: Knowledge will be moved to BC quality after session

features.name: External service controller for API throttling
features.description: A Rust-based external service platform that handles API throttling control when integrating with systems like Shopify, managing rate limits before pushing data to external APIs.
caveats: API throttling handling should be done in external services, not in Business Central
BC is not an integration platform

features.name: JSON parsing in Business Central
features.description: Business Central provides extensive instrumentation to parse and work with JSON payloads, allowing developers to handle JSON mapping directly within BC if a BC developer is available.
caveats: Using data exchange definition for JSON parsing can be slow and resource-intensive

features.name: Data exchange definition for configurable parsing
features.description: A mechanism in Business Central that allows flexible JSON payload mapping, though it can be slow due to hitting multiple tables and is better replaced with direct coding for most use cases.
caveats: Implementation complexity outweighs benefits for field changes
Performance issues when used at scale
Difficult to configure and maintain

features.name: Integration message table pattern
features.description: A standardized single table with type field design for handling multiple integration endpoints, allowing implementation of error handling, scheduling, and retries once for reuse across integrations.
caveats: May require tight coupling with customer systems
Not suitable for all custom scenarios
Handler implementation still needed for payload variations

features.name: Warehouse shipment and receipt integration
features.description: Using Business Central warehouse shipment and receipt documents as the integration point with 3PL systems, providing abstraction for sales orders, purchase orders, returns, and transfer orders.
caveats: Requires not posting documents until 3PL confirms completion
Must handle inventory updates before posting

features.name: Warehouse returns and transfer orders
features.description: Capability to handle return sales returns, purchase returns, and transfer orders between 3PLs using warehouse receipts and shipments without posting until warehouse confirms completion.
caveats: Documents are not posted until warehouse confirms completion

features.name: Webhook abstraction layer for 3PL integrations
features.description: A middleware layer that receives webhook notifications from Business Central and translates them to different 3PL API formats, allowing for decoupling when customers switch between 3PL providers.
caveats: Most 3PLs do not support webhooks natively
3PLs prefer their own API endpoints

features.name: Webhook integration layer
features.description: Integration pattern where warehouse shipments trigger webhooks, allowing external VMS systems to be decoupled and redirected through an integration layer that calls back to Business Central API.
caveats: Not all external systems natively handle webhooks

features.name: Business Central cloud network timeout
features.description: Hard-coded network timeout of 1 minute in Business Central cloud with possibility of 5 minute maximum on premium environments.
caveats: 1 minute hard limit on cloud, proxy side maintains 1 minute, premium environments may support up to 5 minutes

features.name: Job queue categories for message ordering
features.description: Job queue categories feature allows sequencing of background message handling to ensure certain message types are processed before others.
caveats: Prioritization requires custom coding, not built-in prioritization feature

features.name: Integration message code open source
features.description: The integration message code will be made available as open source, allowing customers to customize message handling and prioritization patterns.

features.name: Message table retention policies
features.description: Message retention policy keeps completed messages for one week and failed messages for one month.
